Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of lumbar pain radiating into the
buttock, consistent with the mechanism of injury described. Over the course of care the patient completed 20 visits, a
somewhat longer course than is typical for an uncomplicated lumbar strain. Examination revealed paraspinal muscle
tenderenss and reduced lumbar range of motion, findings that support the reported injury. Neurological screening,
including reflexes, sensation, and straight-leg raise, was within normal limits, and imaging did not show acute
structural abnormality. No prior injury to the lumbar region is documented in the available history. Treatment
consisted of manual therapy, a home exercise program, and graduated activity restrictions, with gradual improvement
in pain and mobility noted over the treatment period. Billed services correspond to the visits performed, with no
duplicated charges identified. Ongoing management includes a return-to-activity plan and reassessment at the next
scheduled follow-up.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
